reuse.why: Rebuilds the existing getScheduledAmount on top of a new shared getWorstCaseAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, but the server sites call the lower-level pieces with their own null/number/range dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three.

duplication.why: The 'null ? 0 : number ? getWorstCaseAmount : getRangedAmount' dispatch is repeated at four sites even though getWorstCaseAmount already dispatches ranges and getScheduledAmount handles null.

placement.why: The rule now lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the existing helper, and the API field is derived in api-models; layering is respected.

scope.why: Mostly on target, but adds four release-notes files (one describing a superseded rule) and updates only Balance.tsx among the client callers that would need the operator.

maintainability.why: Three exported functions (getScheduledAmount, getWorstCaseAmount, getRangedAmount) for one rule, with callers picking different entry points and most client callers not passing the operator, invite drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, forecast-schedules normalizeSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and budget/schedule-template call getWorstCaseAmount/getRangedAmount with their own dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: The per-site 'typeof number ? getWorstCaseAmount(...) : getRangedAmount(...)' ternaries keep the old local dispatch reshaped around new helper names rather than removing it

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter; five server sites (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, normalizeSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, createScheduleList) bypass it via getWorstCaseAmount/getRangedAmount, and client callers other than Balance.tsx omit the op
